title: Cancellation of one split top differential
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $B$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex of $\mathcal O_S$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] supported in $[0,m+1]$ for $m\in\mathbf N$. Suppose its terms are quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], and flat over $\mathrm{id}_S$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. If $B^m\to B^{m+1}$ has a right inverse, there is a cochain complex $D$ supported in $[0,m]$, with all three termwise properties, and a chain homotopy equivalence $D\simeq B$ (chain maps inverse up to degree-minus-one homotopies).

source.place: Tags 068V, 068U, 00NX and 00MT; explicit finite-projective split cancellation argument, expanded by F2

proof.text: Write δ = B.d m (m+1) and choose σ with δ ∘ σ = id. Construct D with ker δ in degree m, B.X j in degrees j < m, and zero above m. Factor the incoming differential into ker δ by the consecutive-differential equation. This gives a complex with support in [0,m]. Define inclusion i:D→B by kernel inclusion in degree m and identities below; define r:B→D using the factorization of id - σ ∘ δ into ker δ in degree m, identities below, and zero above.

Check i and r commute with each differential. At degree m-1 the equality follows from δ ∘ d = 0; at degree m it follows from the defining kernel equation and δ ∘ σ = id. All other equations are identities or maps involving zero objects. The composite r ∘ i is id_D. The degree-minus-one map equal to σ from degree m+1 to m and zero elsewhere has boundary id_B - i ∘ r: at degree m this is σ ∘ δ, at degree m+1 it is δ ∘ σ = id, and elsewhere it is zero. This gives a chain homotopy equivalence D→B, with inverse r.

The changed term ker δ is quasi-coherent by the quasi-coherent kernel theorem. On each affine open its sections are a retract of the sections of B.X m, since id - σ ∘ δ factors through the kernel. Sections of B.X m are finite projective by the affine finite-presentation criterion and flatness over the identity. Retracts remain finite projective, hence finitely presented. The affine criterion gives finite presentation of the kernel sheaf. For flatness over id_S, evaluate the same retraction on every affine pair U⊆V in its defining condition and use Module.Flat.of_retract over Γ(S,V). The unchanged and zero terms have all three properties. Natural m ensures no negative-degree term is introduced, including m = 0.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_split_top_differential_cancellation (S : Scheme.{u})
    (B : CochainComplex S.Modules ℤ) (m : ℕ)
    (hBge : B.IsStrictlyGE 0) (hBle : B.IsStrictlyLE (m + 1 : ℕ))
    (hBflat : ∀ n : ℤ, (B.X n).IsFlatOver (𝟙 S))
    (hBqc : ∀ n : ℤ, (B.X n).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hBfp : ∀ n : ℤ, (B.X n).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hsplit : IsSplitEpi (B.d (m : ℤ) (m + 1 : ℕ))) :
    ∃ D : CochainComplex S.Modules ℤ,
      D.IsStrictlyGE 0 ∧ D.IsStrictlyLE m ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, (D.X n).IsFlatOver (𝟙 S)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, (D.X n).IsQuasicoherent) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, (D.X n).IsFinitePresentation) ∧
      Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv D B)
